title: Ban federal funding of critical race theory training
proposal: The President should issue an executive order banning federal funding of critical race theory training, and Congress should pass a law doing the same.
quote: Issue an executive order banning, and Congress should pass a law prohibiting the federal government from using taxpayer dollars to fund, all critical race theory training (CRT).

title: Direct DOJ and EEOC to enforce Title VII against racial classifications
proposal: The President should direct the Justice Department and the EEOC to enforce Title VII to prohibit racial classifications, quotas, and DEI trainings that promote critical race theory.
quote: direct the Department of Justice and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission to enforce Title VII to prohibit racial classifications and quotas,

title: End EEO-1 race and ethnicity data collection
proposal: The EEOC should stop collecting EEO-1 workforce data by race and ethnicity, and Congress should amend Title VII to bar this and other racial classifications in employment.
quote: work with Congress to amend Title VII to prohibit the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission from collecting EEO-1 data and any other racial classifications

title: Eliminate disparate impact as a theory of discrimination
proposal: Congress should end disparate impact (unequal outcomes without proof of intent) as a valid legal theory of discrimination under Title VII and other laws.
quote: Eliminate disparate impact as a valid theory of discrimination for race and other bases under Title VII and other laws.

title: Bar OFCCP from using disparate impact analysis
proposal: The President should sign an executive order forbidding the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs from using disparate impact in its analysis.
quote: Sign an executive order explicitly forbidding OFCCP from using disparate impact in its analysis.

title: Eliminate OFCCP by rescinding Executive Order 11246
proposal: The President should rescind Executive Order 11246, which would eliminate the office that enforces nondiscrimination rules for federal contractors. Contractors would still follow statutory nondiscrimination law.
quote: Rescind EO 11246. The President should eliminate OFCCP by simply rescinding EO 11246. Federal contractors would still be bound by statutory nondiscrimination law

title: Limit Bostock sex discrimination protections to hiring and firing
proposal: The administration should apply the Supreme Court's Bostock ruling on sexual orientation and transgender status only to hiring and firing decisions.
quote: The new Administration should restrict Bostock’s application of sex discrimination protections to sexual orientation and transgender status in the context of hiring and firing.

title: Withdraw agency guidance applying Bostock beyond hiring and firing
proposal: The President should direct agencies to withdraw notices and guidance that apply Bostock's reasoning outside of hiring and firing.
quote: The President should direct agencies to withdraw unlawful “notices” and “guidances” purporting to apply Bostock’s reasoning broadly outside hiring and firing.

title: Rescind rules treating sexual orientation, gender identity as sex bias
proposal: The President should direct agencies to rescind regulations that read sex discrimination laws as covering sexual orientation, gender identity, transgender status, and sex characteristics.
quote: The President should direct agencies to rescind regulations interpreting sex discrimination provisions as prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity,

title: Enforce sex discrimination laws based on biological sex
proposal: The President should direct agencies to enforce sex discrimination laws using a biological, two-sex meaning of "sex."
quote: The President should direct agencies to focus their enforcement of sex discrimination laws on the biological binary meaning of “sex.”

title: Require equal or greater benefits for pregnancy if abortion is covered
proposal: Congress should require employers that offer abortion benefits to offer equal or greater benefits for pregnancy, childbirth, maternity, and adoption. The law would also say no employer must provide abortion benefits or accommodations.
quote: Congress should pass a law requiring that to the extent an employer provides employee benefits for abortion, it must provide equal or greater benefits for pregnancy,

title: Clarify ERISA does not block state abortion restrictions in benefit plans
proposal: Congress and the Labor Department should clarify that the federal benefits law ERISA does not override state power to restrict abortion, surrogacy, or similar benefits in employer plans.
quote: Congress and DOL should clarify that ERISA does not preempt states’ power to restrict abortion, surrogacy, or other anti-life “benefits.”

title: Executive order protecting religious employers and employees
proposal: The President should issue an executive order saying religious employers may run their businesses by their religious beliefs and supporting their role as federal contractors and program participants.
quote: The President should make clear via executive order that religious employers are free to run their businesses according to their religious beliefs,

title: Expand Title VII religious organization exemptions
proposal: Congress should clarify that religious organizations may make employment decisions based on religion regardless of nondiscrimination laws.
quote: Congress should clarify Title VII’s religious organization exemptions to make it more explicit that those employers may make employment decisions based on religion

title: Raise the bar for denying religious accommodations at work
proposal: Unless the Supreme Court acts, Congress should define "undue hardship" for religious accommodations as significant difficulty or expense, not just more than a small cost.
quote: Congress should clarify that undue hardship means “significant difficulty or expenses,” not “more than a de minimis cost” as the Court has previously held.

title: Require EEOC to act by majority vote of commissioners
proposal: The EEOC should give up claims to regulatory power and make major decisions by a majority vote of commissioners, not by the chair alone or by staff.
quote: EEOC should affirm as policy the Title VII requirement that it exercise substantive power via majority vote of Commissioners, not by unilateral Chair action

title: Limit EEOC consent decrees
proposal: The EEOC should stop entering consent decrees that require employers to do things the law itself does not require.
quote: EEOC should disclaim power to enter into consent decrees that require employer actions that it could not require under the laws it enforces.

title: Shift EEOC priorities to accommodation claims
proposal: The EEOC should focus enforcement on failures to accommodate disability, religion, and pregnancy, but not abortion.
quote: EEOC should reorient its enforcement priorities toward claims of failure to accommodate disability, religion, and pregnancy (but not abortion).

title: Let private workers choose paid time off instead of overtime pay
proposal: Congress should pass the Working Families Flexibility Act so private-sector workers can choose time-and-a-half paid time off instead of overtime pay.
quote: Congress should enact the Working Families Flexibility Act. The Working Families Flexibility Act would allow employees in the private sector the ability to choose

title: Exclude on-site childcare costs from overtime pay rates
proposal: Congress should amend the Fair Labor Standards Act so an employer's cost of on-site childcare does not count toward a worker's regular rate for overtime.
quote: Congress should amend the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) to clarify that an employer’s expenses in providing on-site childcare are not part of an employee’s regular rate of pay.

title: Redirect Women's Bureau research budget
proposal: The Labor Department's Women's Bureau should redirect its research toward open study of women's work participation and the causes of earnings gaps.
quote: The Bureau should rededicate its research budget towards open inquiry, especially to disentangle the influences on women’s workforce participation

title: Double 401(k) contribution limits for married couples
proposal: The contribution limit for married couples on 401(k)-type workplace retirement accounts should be twice the limit for individuals, no matter which spouse works.
quote: the limit for married couples on 401(k) and similar work-based retirement savings accounts should be double the limit for individuals, regardless of the allocation of work between the couple.

title: Create an Assistant Commissioner for Family Statistics at BLS
proposal: Congress should create an Assistant Commissioner for Family Statistics within the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
quote: Congress should establish an Assistant Commissioner for Family Statistics within the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

title: Fund a monthly survey of family well-being
proposal: Congress should require and fund a BLS pilot survey that publishes monthly estimates of how American families are doing.
quote: Congress should require the Bureau to establish a pilot survey with a sample comparable to the BLS Current Population Survey that would publish monthly estimates
contested: An 'Alternative View' in the chapter says monthly family statistics would add little value and funding should instead make annual statistics more timely.

title: Add family-essential goods to the Consumer Price Index
proposal: Congress should require the Consumer Price Index market basket to include measurable family-essential goods.
quote: Congress should require that the Consumer Price Index market basket include measurable family-essential goods.

title: Require time-and-a-half pay for work on the Sabbath
proposal: Congress should amend the Fair Labor Standards Act to require time-and-a-half pay for hours worked on the Sabbath, which would default to Sunday, with some exemptions.
quote: amending the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA)9 to require that workers be paid time and a half for hours worked on the Sabbath.
contested: Proposed by the chapter author; an 'Alternative View' in the chapter opposes it, saying it would raise costs and that government should remove barriers rather than add them.

title: Change overtime rules for teleworkers
proposal: Congress should say teleworkers earn overtime only if they work more than 10 hours in a day and more than 40 hours in the week.
quote: Congress should clarify that overtime for telework applies only if the employee exceeds 10 hours of work in a specific day (and the total hours for the week exceed 40).

title: Ease time-tracking rules for teleworkers
proposal: The Labor Department should say teleworkers need to record time only when their assigned work for the day is more than usual.
quote: DOL should clarify that an employee given the option to telework need only record time if the quantity of work assigned for that day exceeds the usual amount

title: Exempt home offices from OSHA rules
proposal: The Labor Department should clarify that home offices are not covered by OSHA rules, that setting one up is not paid work time, and that home office reimbursements do not raise overtime pay rates.
quote: DOL should clarify that a home office is not subject to OSHA regulations and that time to set up a home office is not compensable time

title: Restore Trump-era independent contractor rules
proposal: The NLRB and Labor Department should go back to their 2019 and 2021 rules defining who is an independent contractor.
quote: NLRB and DOL should return to their 2019 and 2021 independent contractor rules that provided much-needed clarity for workers and employers.

title: Create one legal test for employee vs. contractor status
proposal: Congress should set a single bright-line test, based on how much control a worker has over the work, to decide employee or contractor status under all federal laws.
quote: Congress should establish a bright-line test—based on the level of control an individual exercises over his or her work—to determine whether a payee is an employee

title: Safe harbor for offering benefits to independent workers
proposal: Congress should let companies offer benefits to independent workers without that making them employers.
quote: Congress should provide a safe harbor from employer-employee status for companies that offer independent workers access to earned benefits.

title: Narrow the joint employer definition
proposal: The Labor Department and NLRB should define joint employers based on direct and immediate control over workers.
quote: DOL and NLRB should return to the long-standing approach to defining joint employers based on direct and immediate control.

title: Pass the Save Local Business Act
proposal: Congress should pass the Save Local Business Act to write the narrower joint employer definition into law.
quote: Congress should enact the Save Local Business Act, which would codify the long-standing definition that has existed outside the Obama-era and Biden-proposed rules.

title: Keep overtime salary threshold near Trump-era level
proposal: The Labor Department should keep an overtime salary threshold that does not burden businesses in lower-cost regions, such as the Trump-era level.
quote: DOL should maintain an overtime threshold that does not punish businesses in lower-cost regions (e.g., the southeast United States).

title: Base overtime pay on salary, not benefits
proposal: Congress should clarify that the "regular rate" used to figure overtime pay is based on salary, not all benefits.
quote: Congress should clarify that the “regular rate” for overtime pay is based on the salary paid rather than all benefits provided.

title: Allow overtime to be calculated over two or four weeks
proposal: Congress should let employers and workers figure overtime over a two- or four-week period instead of a single week.
quote: Specifically, employers and employees should be able to set a two- or four-week period over which to calculate overtime.

title: Restore limits on agency guidance documents
proposal: The Labor Department should bring back its PRO Good Guidance rule limiting the use of guidance, and Congress should amend the Administrative Procedure Act to limit guidance documents.
quote: DOL should reinstitute the PRO Good Guidance rule via notice and comment.

title: Exempt small businesses from labor rules where possible
proposal: Labor agencies should use the Regulatory Flexibility Act to exempt small entities from regulations where they can.
quote: The labor agencies should exercise their available discretion and duties under the Regulatory Flexibility Act

title: Raise NLRB jurisdiction thresholds for inflation
proposal: Congress should raise the revenue levels at which the NLRB covers employers to account for inflation since 1935.
quote: Congress should enact legislation increasing the revenue thresholds at which the National Labor Relations Board asserts jurisdiction over employers to match changes in inflation

title: Waive OSHA fines for first-time small business violators
proposal: Congress, and the Labor Department through enforcement discretion, should exempt small businesses with first-time, non-willful violations from OSHA fines.
quote: Congress (and DOL, in its enforcement discretion) should exempt small business, first-time, non-willful violators from fines issued by the Occupational Health and Safety Administration.

title: Restore industry-recognized apprenticeship programs
proposal: The administration should create an industry-recognized apprenticeship program separate from Registered Apprenticeships, and Congress should re-create this system in law.
quote: implement an industry-recognized apprenticeship program separate from the Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) and explore how best to modernize, streamline, and eliminate duplication in the RAP

title: Involve religious organizations in apprenticeships
proposal: The Labor Department and NLRB should help religious organizations take part in apprenticeships, worker organizations, job training, and benefits networks.
quote: Both DOL and NLRB should facilitate religious organizations helping to strengthen working families via apprenticeship programs, worker organizations, vocational training,

title: Let trained teens work in some hazardous jobs
proposal: The Labor Department should change its hazard-order rules so teenagers with proper training and parental consent can work in some dangerous jobs.
quote: DOL should amend its hazard-order regulations to permit teenage workers access to work in regulated jobs with proper training and parental consent.

title: Create employer grants for on-the-job training
proposal: Congress should create grants of up to $10,000 per year per worker for employers running formal on-the-job training, paid for with money from higher education subsidies.
quote: Congress should create an employer grant worth up to $10,000 per year or pro-rated portion thereof for each worker engaged in

title: Skills-based hiring for federal contractors
proposal: The President should direct federal procurement officials to apply civil service skills-based hiring standards to contractors and waive degree requirements in existing contracts.
quote: The President should direct the Administrator for Federal Procurement Policy to adopt the civil service’s skills-based hiring standards for federal contractors
agency: OMB / Office of Federal Procurement Policy

title: Ban bachelor's degree requirements in private job listings
proposal: Congress should bar private employers from requiring a bachelor's degree in job descriptions or algorithm screening, unless the degree is a real job requirement.
quote: Congress should prohibit the inclusion of a BA requirement in job descriptions for all private sector employers, or the use of a BA requirement to screen applicants
contested: Proposed in the main text; an 'Alternative View' in the chapter says the government should not decide whether private employers can require degrees.

title: Streamline federal job training programs in WIOA reauthorization
proposal: When renewing the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, Congress should remove overlap among job training programs and tie their funding to results.
quote: Congress should evaluate and streamline the existing workforce development programs to ensure there is no overlap or fragmentation between programs.

title: Require outcome measures in job training programs
proposal: The Labor Department and other agencies should review training programs, require outcome-based measures, reconsider funding for weak programs, and sanction bad-actor grantees.
quote: DOL and other federal agencies with jurisdiction over employment and training programs should review their programs and utilize all available tools and authority

title: Tighten unemployment insurance fraud controls
proposal: Congress should let the Labor Department's Inspector General access all state unemployment records and require states to check applicants against the National Directory of New Hires.
quote: including statutory authority for the Labor Office of Inspector General (OIG) to access all state UI records for the purposes of investigation and requiring state agencies to crossmatch

title: Develop technology standards for state unemployment systems
proposal: Congress should commission a report setting technical standards for state unemployment systems, such as cybersecurity and identity checks.
quote: Congress should also develop a framework (through commission of a congressional report to serve as a blueprint) of technical standards

title: Give DOL more enforcement tools over state UI programs
proposal: Congress should give the Labor Department more measured tools to enforce unemployment insurance rules than a letter or removing a state's whole tax credit.
quote: Congress should provide DOL with more reasonable enforcement tools for the UI system.

title: Review $2 billion in pandemic UI modernization spending
proposal: The Labor Department should review all planned spending of $2 billion from the American Rescue Plan for unemployment fraud detection, access, and equity, and improve state monitoring.
quote: DOL should review all actual or planned procurements against the $2 billion (under the American Rescue Plan Act)

title: Allow non-union worker-management groups (TEAM Act)
proposal: Congress should pass the TEAM Act to allow "Employee Involvement Organizations" for worker-management cooperation and let them elect a non-voting board member at large public companies.
quote: Congress should reintroduce and pass the Teamwork for Employees and Managers (TEAM) Act of 2022.
contested: Proposed by the chapter author; an 'Alternative View' doubts workers lack a voice and favors the Worker's Choice Act instead.

title: End exclusive union representation in right-to-work states
proposal: An alternative view in the chapter supports the Worker's Choice Act, which would end exclusive representation so unions need not represent workers who do not join.
quote: this by ending exclusive representation so that unions in right-to-work states are no longer forced to represent workers who do not want to join them.
contested: Offered as an 'Alternative View' by other conservatives, not the chapter author's main recommendation.

title: Require more union financial disclosure
proposal: The Intermediate Bodies Rule, requiring some government-worker unions to file financial reports, should become law, and the T-1 union trust report should be restored.
quote: The substance of the Intermediate Bodies Rule should pass into law, either through rulemaking or through legislation. The T-1 Trust Annual Report annual filing requirement should be restored.

title: Increase funding for the Office of Labor-Management Standards
proposal: Congress should increase funding for the office that enforces union disclosure laws.
quote: Increase funding levels. Congress should expand the funding of the Office of Labor-Management Standards.

title: Treat union political conflicts as breach of fair representation
proposal: The NLRB should argue that union leaders' political conflicts of interest can support claims that a union broke its duty of fair representation.
quote: The NLRB should take enforcement or amicus action advancing the position that political conflicts of interest by union leadership can support claims for breach

title: Narrow what counts as protected concerted activity
proposal: The NLRB should return to its 2019 Alstate Maintenance standard for what worker activity is protected under labor law.
quote: The NLRB should return to the 2019 Alstate Maintenance interpretation of what does and does not constitute protected concerted activity,

title: Seek more court orders to reinstate fired organizers
proposal: The NLRB should more often seek 10(j) injunctions to quickly reinstate workers fired for organizing, and set guidelines for doing so.
quote: The NLRB should increase its use of 10(j) and should articulate guidelines for situations in which it intends to seek injunctive relief;

title: Require worker centers to file union-style financial reports
proposal: The Labor Department should investigate worker centers that act like unions and take enforcement action to make them file the same financial disclosures.
quote: DOL should investigate worker centers that look and act like unions and bring enforcement actions to require them to file the same financial disclosures.

title: Let OLMS investigate unions without a complaint
proposal: The Office of Labor-Management Standards should change its rules so it can investigate possible union wrongdoing without a formal complaint.
quote: The Office of Labor-Management Standards should revise its investigation standards to authorize investigations without receiving a formal complaint.

title: Rescind the persuader rule if revived
proposal: If the persuader rule on disclosing advice to employers about unions is revived, the Labor Department should rescind it again.
quote: DOL should rescind the persuader rule once again should the Biden Administration revive it.

title: Require secret-ballot elections for union recognition
proposal: Congress should end "card check" union recognition and require secret-ballot elections only.
quote: Congress should discard “card check” as the basis of union recognition and mandate the secret ballot exclusively.

title: Eliminate the union contract bar rule
proposal: The NLRB should end the contract bar rule so workers have a fair chance to vote out a union.
quote: NLRB should eliminate the contract bar rule so that employees with an interest in decertification have a reasonable chance to achieve their goal.

title: Let union contracts adjust national employment rules
proposal: Congress should amend the National Labor Relations Act so union contracts can treat national employment laws, like overtime rules, as negotiable defaults.
quote: Congress should amend the NLRA to authorize collective bargaining to treat national employment laws and regulations as negotiable defaults.

title: End mandatory Project Labor Agreements
proposal: Agencies should end required Project Labor Agreements on federal construction and choose contractors on quality and cost.
quote: Agencies should end all mandatory Project Labor Agreement requirements and base federal procurement decisions on the contractors that can deliver the best product at the lowest cost.
contested: Offered as an 'Alternative Policy' by other conservatives; the chapter author says it would be a mistake to antagonize unions' core interests.

title: Repeal the Davis-Bacon Act
proposal: Congress should repeal the Davis-Bacon Act, which requires "prevailing wages" on federally funded construction, and let markets set wages.
quote: Repeal Davis–Bacon. Congress should enact the Davis–Bacon Repeal Act and allow markets to determine market wages.
contested: Offered as an 'Alternative Policy' by other conservatives; the chapter author says it would be a mistake to antagonize unions' core interests.

title: Allow private worker organizations to run unemployment benefits
proposal: The Labor Department should approve non-government worker organizations to administer unemployment insurance.
quote: DOL should approve, pursuant to § 303(a)(2) of the Social Security Act, non-public worker organizations as administrators.

title: Offer state waivers for unemployment insurance alternatives
proposal: The Labor Department should grant waivers from standard unemployment rules to states that propose suitable alternatives.
quote: DOL should offer waivers from the standard requirements imposed on unemployment compensation by § 303(a) and § 303(d) of the Social Security Act to states that propose suitable

title: Limit political spending by groups receiving UI funds
proposal: The Labor Department should require organizations receiving public funds to follow the same political spending limits as 501(c)(3) charities.
quote: DOL should establish as a precondition for receiving any public funds a requirement that an organization comply with restrictions on political spending

title: Allow state waivers from federal labor laws
proposal: Congress should let states and localities get time-limited waivers from federal labor laws like the NLRA and FLSA if their reforms meet the laws' purposes.
quote: Congress should pass legislation allowing waivers from federal labor laws like the NLRA and FLSA under certain conditions.

title: Keep federally funded licensing compacts from adding requirements
proposal: Congress should ensure federally funded interstate licensing compacts do not add qualifications beyond what states require.
quote: Congress should ensure that interstate compacts for occupational license recognition that are federally funded do not require new or additional qualifications

title: Stop federal programs from locking qualified licensees out of work
proposal: Congress should make sure federally funded programs, such as limited Medicare-funded medical residencies, do not keep qualified licensees out of jobs.
quote: Congress should ensure that well-qualified licensees are not locked out of the job market by restrictive government programs funded by the federal government.

title: Restore state staffing flexibility for job service programs
proposal: The Labor Department should reissue the Trump-era rule letting states use contractors for Wagner-Peyser job services, and Congress should write it into law.
quote: DOL should repromulgate the Trump-era staffing flexibility rule, and Congress should codify it.

title: Bar ESG investing in workplace retirement plans
proposal: The Labor Department should prohibit ERISA retirement plans from investing based on factors unrelated to risk and return, returning to a pecuniary-only standard.
quote: DOL should prohibit investing in ERISA plans on the basis of any factors that are unrelated to investor risks and returns.
contested: An 'Alternative View' notes some conservatives want all non-financial factors banned, while others think plans may offer ESG options that individuals choose.

title: Scrutinize retirement plan investments in China
proposal: The Labor Department should consider enforcement or rules to closely examine ERISA plan investments in China.
quote: DOL should consider taking enforcement and/or regulatory action to subject investment in China to greater scrutiny under ERISA.

title: Remove ESG mutual fund windows from the federal TSP
proposal: The Labor Department should remove mutual fund options in the federal Thrift Savings Plan that encourage ESG investing and clarify its fiduciary duties.
quote: DOL should reverse efforts to politicize the TSP by removing “mutual fund” windows that encourage ESG, and should clarify the fiduciary duties of the TSP

title: Replace BlackRock and State Street as TSP managers
proposal: The federal government should move Thrift Savings Plan funds away from BlackRock and State Street and hire a different competitive private manager.
quote: removing their pension funds from fund managers such as BlackRock and State Street Global Advisers, and contract with a competitive, private-sector manager

title: Consider enforcement against TSP fund managers
proposal: The Labor Department should consider enforcement actions against BlackRock and State Street for fiduciary violations while managing the TSP.
quote: DOL should also consider bringing enforcement actions against BlackRock and State Street Global Advisers for their violations of fiduciary duty while managing the TSP

title: Let the TSP board vote its own proxies
proposal: Congress should authorize the Thrift Savings Plan board to use its own judgment on proxy votes and give it clear voting guidelines.
quote: Congress should enact legislation authorizing the FRTIB to exercise its independent business judgment in exercising the proxy votes for its holdings of the TSP

title: Prohibit TSP investments in China
proposal: The Labor Department should use its oversight to bar Thrift Savings Plan investments in China, and Congress should ban them by law.
quote: DOL should exercise its oversight of the FRTIB to prohibit investments in China.

title: Require public pension plans to disclose market-value funding
proposal: Congress should require state and local pension funds to report the fair market value of assets and liabilities each year, using Treasury rates.
quote: Congress should require public pension funds to disclose the fair market value of plan assets and liabilities (using the Treasury yield curve as the discount rate)

title: Reform multiemployer union pension plans
proposal: Congress should give multiemployer pension participants the same protections as single-employer plans, divide liabilities among employers, and bar troubled plans from new promises.
quote: Congress should reform multiemployer pensions to give participants in these plans the same protections as those in single-employer plans.

title: Require timely PBGC annual reports
proposal: The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation's annual report should be on time and use current, fair-market data.
quote: The PBGC’s annual report must be submitted on time, and with timely data that uses fair-market value principles to calculate the PBGC’s finances.

title: Have PBGC act on badly run multiemployer plans
proposal: The PBGC should closely monitor underfunded multiemployer plans and take remedial action, including ending plans where appropriate.
quote: The PBGC should use existing statutory authority to protect workers, retirees, employers, and taxpayers by closely monitoring and taking appropriate remedial action

title: Raise PBGC premiums on underfunded pension plans
proposal: Congress should raise the premium on pension underfunding, remove the per-person cap, lower the flat premium, and raise multiemployer premiums to match single-employer plans.
quote: Congress should increase the variable rate premium on underfunding and eliminate the per-participant cap in order to appropriately take into account risk

title: Issue clear rules for employee stock ownership plans
proposal: The Labor Department should issue clear rules on ESOP valuation and fiduciary conduct to make it easier for employers to offer them.
quote: DOL should make it easier for employers to offer ESOPs by providing clear regulations for ESOP valuation and fiduciary conduct
contested: An 'Alternative View' says some conservatives think government should not favor one type of investment over another.

title: Cap and phase down the H-2A farmworker visa
proposal: Congress should cap H-2A temporary farmworker visas at current levels and phase the program down over 10 to 20 years.
quote: Congress should immediately cap this program at its current levels and establish a schedule for its gradual and predictable phasedown over the subsequent 10 to 20 years,
contested: Proposed in the main text; an 'Alternative View' says H-2A fills jobs Americans will not take and keeps food prices down.

title: Match industry funding for farm automation research
proposal: Congress should encourage an industry group of farm equipment and robotics firms and match its funding, with shared intellectual property.
quote: Congress should also encourage the establishment of an industry consortium of agricultural equipment producers and other automation and robotics firms

title: Phase out the H-2B seasonal worker visa
proposal: Congress should cap H-2B seasonal nonfarm worker visas at current levels and phase them out over no more than 10 years.
quote: Congress should immediately cap this program at its current levels and establish a schedule for its gradual and predictable phasedown over no more than 10 years.
contested: Proposed in the main text; an 'Alternative View' says H-2B fills seasonal jobs businesses cannot otherwise staff.

title: Require federal contractors to employ mostly U.S. citizens
proposal: Congress should require new federal contracts to have at least 70 percent U.S. citizen employees, rising to at least 95 percent over 10 years.
quote: Congress should mandate that all new federal contracts require at least 70 percent of the contractor’s employees to be U.S. citizens,
contested: Proposed in the main text; an 'Alternative View' says contract staffing should be based on economy and efficiency, not quotas.

title: Allow employers to prefer citizens in hiring
proposal: Congress should change the law so employers may prefer U.S. citizens over work-authorized noncitizens when hiring, which has been illegal since 1986.
quote: Congress must amend the law so that employers can again have the freedom to make hiring Americans a priority.

title: Speed debarment of employers who commit visa fraud
proposal: The Labor Department should follow its Inspector General's advice and investigate visa fraud more strongly and debar guilty employers faster.
quote: institute more robust investigations for suspected visa fraud and speedier debarments for those found guilty.

title: Copy USMCA labor protections in future trade deals
proposal: The U.S. Trade Representative should include USMCA-style labor provisions in future trade agreements, such as banning forced labor and a rapid-response enforcement panel.
quote: For future FTAs, the USTR should replicate the labor provisions of USMCA, especially the provisions to:

title: Add forced labor and supply-chain rules to trade authority
proposal: For future Trade Promotion Authority, the President should urge Congress to require supply-chain transparency and a general ban on forced labor conditions.
quote: For future authorizations of Trade Promotion Authority (TPA), the President should urge Congress to:

title: Focus international labor investigations on harms to U.S. workers
proposal: The Labor Department's Bureau of International Labor Affairs should focus on foreign labor abuses that most hurt American workers' earnings, like child and forced labor.
quote: The next Administration should focus ILAB investigations on foreign labor violations that do the most to damage American workers’ earning power,

title: Cut Labor Department budget to about $10.9 billion
proposal: Labor agency budgets should be cut to the low end of historical levels, such as the $10.9 billion requested for FY 2020, mostly from the Employment and Training Administration.
quote: Reduce the agencies’ budgets to the low end of the historical average. The Trump Administration’s FY 2020 request, $10.9 billion, would provide a workable target

title: Focus safety inspections on egregious offenders
proposal: Health and safety inspections should focus on the worst offenders.
quote: Focus health and safety inspections on egregious offenders, as other inspections are often abused and usurp state and local government prerogatives.

title: Maximize political appointees at the Labor Department
proposal: The Labor Department should have as many political appointees as possible.
quote: The number of political appointees should be maximized in order to improve the political accountability of the department.

title: Replace EEOC and NLRB general counsels on Day One
proposal: The next administration should replace the EEOC and NLRB general counsels right away and decline to recognize fixed terms in other offices where applicable.
quote: The next Administration should do the same and expand on the Biden Administration’s new precedent by refusing to acknowledge terms in other offices,

title: Freeze hiring of career staff
proposal: The labor agencies should put a hiring freeze on career officials.
quote: Implement a hiring freeze for career officials. A hiring freeze imposes financial discipline on agencies’ personnel costs and reduces agency bloat.

title: Fully staff the Office of Compliance Initiatives
proposal: The Labor Department should fully staff its office that helps employers and workers understand labor rules.
quote: DOL should fully staff the Office of Compliance Initiatives (OCI), which was reopened by the Trump Administration

title: Move foreign labor certification office under the Secretary
proposal: The Office of Foreign Labor Certification should be moved out of the Employment and Training Administration and report to the Secretary under a political director.
quote: OFLC should be moved out of ETA and made directly accountable to the Secretary with a politically accountable Director.
